correctness.rationale: The simultaneous inverse-shuffle coupling is established in the primary preprint. Direct enumeration of all shared-index inversion–descent covariances gives the exact affine site formula. Its endpoints yield an if-and-only-if sign threshold. Exact variance calculations give the limiting covariance matrix. The centered Bernoulli expansion separates inversion count into a weighted independent sum and a quadratic degenerate remainder of variance O(n²); bounded one-dependent blocking plus Cramér–Wold proves the joint limit. The matrix determinant q²(1-12q²)/12 is positive for 0<q≤1/4. The actual standalone package verifier passed 702 exact checks across 2≤n≤9, including independently sampled forward-cut/interleaving distributions for n≤7. Neither finite checks nor marginal normality is substituted for the all-n proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Fixed-composition moment tools may algebraically imply some finite covariance coefficients after mixing over composition, and that portion is not represented as an independent deep theorem. They do not by themselves prove the joint limit for the randomly cut biased shuffle or the exact site-wise sign threshold. Major index weights descent positions; it is not the unweighted descent number. Full-text nonaccess to Thiel remains a stated residual risk, not a certification of noncoverage.

value.rationale: This is a natural two-statistic question for a standard nonuniform card-shuffling model already studied in the primary literature. The exact site-level mixed-covariance sign transition isolates a concrete finite-size crossover absent from marginal variances. The joint CLT quantifies a nonzero persistence of dependence under deck-length growth and characterizes a unique independence symmetry of the limiting Gaussian law. These are natural structure and limit laws with direct statistical interpretation, not arbitrary low-n computations.
